paragraphs: Elazar ben Dordaya, Avodah Zarah 17a: he had visited every prostitute. Hearing of one overseas charging a purse of dinars, he took it and crossed seven rivers. During intercourse she passed wind: “As this wind cannot return, so Elazar ben Dordaya will not be accepted in repentance.” He sat among mountains and hills: “Ask mercy for me.” “Before asking for you, we must ask for ourselves: ‘The mountains shall depart,’” etc. Heaven, earth, sun, moon, stars, constellations likewise answered his plea, etc. “It depends only on me.” Head between knees, he wept until his soul departed. A heavenly voice: “Rabbi Elazar ben Dordaya is destined for the world to come.” Rabbi wept: “Some acquire their world in one hour—and they call him Rabbi!” Repentance comes from understanding, “His heart shall understand, return, and be healed”; the penitent is wise, hence Rabbi and the world to come. According to the later tradition, he was a reincarnation of Yochanan the high priest, who served eighty years and became a Sadducee. Thus Rabbi wept: one hour acquires what Yochanan labored eighty years for, K.Sh., chapter 19 [ק״ש; work unresolved]. That is, Yochanan lost in one hour eighty years’ labor; Elazar reversed it.
